newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle futures end mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle futures end mostly higher.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed mostly higher as stronger cash indications and evening up ahead of Friday's USDA cattle report combined to lift prices, traders said.

Active boxed beef movement Wednesday and Thursday led to ideas of firmer fed cattle markets going into next week. Feedlots are also showing continued tight near-term feedlot numbers which added to strength in nearby live cattle futures, traders said.
However, the report is expected to show rising fed numbers which weighed on deferred months, they said.

Analysts' estimates for October 1 on-feed cattle supplies at major feedlots in Friday's monthly report averaged 94.8 percent of a year ago and ranged from 93.8 to 97 percent. However, September placement estimates averaged 98.6 in a range of 96.2 to 104 percent and compare with large placements last year. Marketing estimates averaged 87.8 percent of a year ago and ranged from 85 to 90.8 percent.
Refco spread long December/short February and long December/short October. RBH was also a notable buyer of December, pit sources said.
